primary_reason: Residual income valuation adds no incremental information over book-to-price, and perfect foresight does not rescue it. X2 shows RIM V/P does rank constituent returns (mean IC +0.199 all origins, +0.292 window-complete, CI excluding zero on both) but plain B/P ranks them better at every origin set (+0.256 / +0.335), so the entire apparatus subtracts about 0.05 of IC. X3 shows that even an Oracle arm fed the realised future book and earnings of all 30 constituents fails the frozen bar (rho +0.231, CI [-0.030, 0.449], n=13), which closes the hypothesis that better forecast data would fix it.
evidence: X3 Oracle fails: knowing the actual future does not rank subsequent returns to the frozen standard (window-complete rho +0.231, CI lower bound -0.030). No purchasable forecast dataset can supply better inputs than the realised outcome, so cost was never the binding constraint.
X3 Deployable fails harder (+0.033, CI [-0.262, 0.322]); matrix key oracle_fail_deployable_fail resolves to RIM_STRUCTURE_UNSUITED_TO_THE_TARGET.
X2 incremental criterion fails on both origin sets: V/P minus B/P is -0.057 (all 34) and -0.043 (window-complete 18).

E1 terminated top-down B1: the model ranks below the same-origin historical P/B baseline on all four US indices, and that verdict survived X0's window-completeness recheck (full-window baselines 0.72-0.84 against the model's 0.15-0.64).

X0 established the current implementation is not the literature's RIM at all: consensus null at every origin, 6 of 7 components MATERIAL_DEVIATION against Frankel-Lee, the Dow bottom-up and Dechow. What was tested is a historical-accounting B1 heuristic, per contract 8.1.

X0 also voided E2's apparent pass: the '34/34 truncated' flag was a tautology, real truncation is 18 of 34, and on window-complete origins the baseline beats bottom-up (+0.447 vs +0.302) rather than losing to it.

X1 confirmed the period was hostile to value (HML -20.7%, Big Value minus Big Growth -44.4%) and found a positive factor-residual signal on the clean subset (+0.501, CI [0.331, 0.726]) - but its own frozen interpretability bar fired INSUFFICIENT_MATCHED_UNIVERSE at R2 0.490 against 0.50, and effective n there is 11.3.
rejected_alternatives: BUILD_VALIDATED_BOTTOM_UP_RIM - contract section 9A requires positive cross-sectional information AND incremental value over baseline AND a passing deployable arm. The first holds, the second and third do not.

REQUIRES_PAID_POINT_IN_TIME_FORECAST_DATA - the owner ruled out purchase, and independently X3's Oracle failure makes the purchase moot: the data would not fix a formula that fails with perfect foresight. The provider survey is retained as the record that FactSet and S&P sell exactly this, publish no price, and were not needed.

Adding a multiple-expansion term - forbidden by the owner ruling and by the contract; in RIM the market-to-book gap is already supposed to be explained by future residual income, and a separate term reintroduces double counting and result fitting.

Re-running with a looser criterion - three frozen bars were missed by small margins (X1 R2 by 0.01, X3 Oracle CI by 0.030, X2 incremental by 0.043). Moving any of them after seeing the numbers is the exact failure mode the contract forbids.
next_action: Redesign the public valuation surface as an ensemble of independent lenses per contract section 9C - historical P/E and P/B percentiles, earnings yield against rates, Yardeni, ERP spread, long-run earnings normalisation, revisions and breadth - showing agreement and disagreement between methods rather than one unvalidated fair-value band. X2 supplies a concrete starting point: book-to-price carries a mean IC of +0.26 to +0.34 on this basket, so the simple lens the ensemble would use is measurably the stronger one. Move the RIM engine, the Yoo structure reproduction and the full audit trail to a research archive; preserve, do not delete. Backlog #380 - the point-in-time estimate archive - remains the highest-value follow-up because every failure in this track traced to data that existed at the time and was not kept.
